newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index boosted by foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index boosted by foreign demand.

text.p: Foreign investor demand for key shares at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) maintained the bourse's bullish tone on Tuesday, bourse officials said.
The NSE's 20-share index gained 42.65 points to stand at 3671.63. Turnover was posted at 30.266 million shillings on 672,108 shares from 20.110 million shillings on 432,972 shares.
"As you can see prices are still going up but generally today foreign investors dominated the market," a senior broker said.
They bought some 31,000 shares of Sasini Tea & Coffee at 69-75 from 66 and 23,300 shares of Kenya Commercial Bank at 85-88 from 85.
Bourse officials and brokers said there was an air of excitement in the market on Tuesday as many investors are buying heavily in anticipation of end-year results due February.
"But by the second week of February, I think prices should go down because most companies will have made their announcements," another broker said.
All eyes are on this week's star performer Total Kenya which edged up a further 3.0 to close at 97, a total gain of 16 since Friday, on good end-year results to be announced very soon.
Financials gained marginally with Barclays Bank closing at 129 from 128, while Housing Finance Company eased to 24.50 from 25.
Foreign investors also bought some 1,600 shares of Firestone East Africa at 30 from 30.25 and 29,300 shares of Kenya Breweries at 53 from 52.
Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting shed 45 to close at 294.
Some three million shillings worth of East African Development Bank floating-rate bonds changed hands at 104.324 percent.
